`vcs.status()` includes untracked files, but `git stash push -m ...` does not stash untracked files by default. This can leave untracked changes behind when warping, even though the UI says “Uncommitted changes stashed”. Consider including untracked files in the stash to match the status check and user expectation.

DesktopIpcContract’s request/response types don’t match the existing Electron IPC surface in this repo. For example, get/set-display-backend is typed as string | null, but preload/types.ts defines LinuxDisplayBackend ("wayland" | "auto") for these calls, and the store-* channels are currently invoked/handled with positional args (name, key, value), not a single object payload. As written, the contract would be incorrect if adopted and would reintroduce mismatches rather than preventing them.

invokeIpcWith/handleIpcWith currently hardcode a single `request` argument (`ipcRenderer.invoke(channel, request)` / `(event, request)`), but several existing channels use multiple positional args (e.g. store-get/store-set). This wrapper would silently mis-handle those channels. It also relies on `any`, which undermines the “typed bridge” goal.

The contract currently forces callers to pass `undefined` for void-request channels (and this test encodes that behavior). If invokeIpcWith is updated to use rest-args/tuple requests (so void-request channels take 0 args, matching existing ipcRenderer.invoke usage), update this test to assert the 0-arg call pattern.

PR description claims an “end-to-end typed IPC contract bridge … for desktop IPC calls between preload and main”, but DesktopIpcContract currently covers only a small subset of the channels that are already used/handled (e.g. install-cli, updater-*, wsl-servers-*, open-file-picker, window/zoom/titlebar, etc.). As a result, most IPC calls remain untyped and unprotected from channel/parameter mismatches unless the contract is expanded (or the PR description is narrowed).
